data.title: Zoomlion Chairman Zhan Chunxin Meets Australian Customers to Strengthen Long-Term Partnerships
data.description:
SYDNEY, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zoomlion Heavy Industry Science & Technology Co., Ltd. ("Zoomlion" or "the Company") Chairman and CEO Mr. Zhan Chunxin met with Australian customers in Sydney on Nov. 4 to discuss product quality, technical support, spare parts availability, and local training. The meeting also covered opportunities for closer cooperation in Australia.

Customers and partners from the tower crane, concrete machinery, earthmoving, aerial work platform, agricultural machinery, and financial sectors attended, along with Zoomlion Co-President Wang Yongxiang, Vice President Hu Keman, and Employee Representative Director Liu Xiaoping. Zhan thanked customers and partners for their longstanding cooperation.

During the discussions, Zhan emphasised Australia's importance as a strategic market for Zoomlion and reiterated the Company's commitment to long-term development in Australia. He also invited participating customers to visit the Zoomlion Smart City in Changsha, China, to learn more about the Company's manufacturing and technological capabilities.

How does Zoomlion support customers in Australia?

Zoomlion has expanded its operations to five regional business centres in Sydney, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, and Adelaide since entering the Australian market in 2008. Originally set up as sales support locations, these sites have gradually taken on a broader role as regional business centres. The company now offers equipment across all its product categories in Australia. Through increased investment in the country in 2026, Zoomlion strengthened its service network and extended coverage beyond major regional hubs to make local support more accessible and improve its ability to respond to service requests.

These efforts form part of Zoomlion's broader global customer service initiative, which includes more than 30 local service hotlines supported by a global call centre. Australian customers can request technical assistance through their local hotline, and Zoomlion's service teams can coordinate repairs, spare parts, and on-site support.

Participating customers welcomed the opportunity to engage directly with Zoomlion's senior leadership. They said the visit reflected the importance Zoomlion placed on the Australian market. They praised the Company's product quality, technical support, and local services and expressed confidence in the prospects for further cooperation. Wang reaffirmed Zoomlion's commitment to its Australian partners by highlighting plans to expand local investment and strengthen the delivery of technology, equipment, and services tailored to customer requirements.

Moving forward, Zoomlion will continue investing in its Australian service network to make local support more accessible and build on longstanding customer relationships.

data.title: Kenya chooses US consortium to develop Mrima Hill critical minerals project
data.description:
By Ammu Kannampilly and Aaron Ross

Kenya said it has chosen a group that includes American rare earths startup ReElement Technologies to develop its Mrima Hill critical minerals deposit, handing the US a coveted prize in its bid to bolster supplies of minerals used in defence and electronics.

US officials have described Mrima Hill in southeastern Kenya as a key target in the campaign by US President Donald Trump's administration to increase American access to critical minerals, whose processing is dominated by China.

Kenya's mining ministry says preliminary indicators suggest Mrima Hill contains tens of billions of dollars’ worth of rare earth minerals as well as niobium, a metal used in aerospace manufacturing.

The ministry said in a statement on Thursday that it had selected the Frontier Minerals consortium, which includes Indiana-based ReElement and US-based miner Bunker Hill Silver Corp , in an open and transparent process.

The winner will now have to engage with the local community and obtain prospecting licences, it added.

The news was first reported by Reuters.

Seven bidders — including two Chinese companies, two US consortia, one US-affiliated consortium, ​an Australian consortium and a Kenyan-British joint venture — were shortlisted in July. The Chinese companies later withdrew from the process without stating a reason.

ReElement aims to use a novel processing technology to refine rare earths and other critical minerals. Reuters reported in July that the company stopped seeking an $80 million loan from the US Department of Defense after struggling to satisfy due diligence issues.

The company was later given a $25 million grant from the Pentagon to buy equipment for its Indiana processing site.

Toronto-listed Bunker Hill is building operations at a zinc, silver and lead mine in the US state of Idaho.
